stem: A client who has taken clozapine for 6 weeks calls the clinic with a temperature of 101.5°F (38.6°C), chills, and a new sore throat. Which nursing response best reflects current clozapine safety guidance?

options.A: Advise the client to continue clozapine until the next scheduled weekly blood count because routine ANC monitoring during the first 6 months is sufficient unless symptoms worsen.
options.B: Instruct the client to interrupt clozapine and arrange prompt clinical evaluation with an ANC because fever at or above 101.3°F (38.5°C) during treatment requires this response.
options.C: Advise the client to continue clozapine and treat the symptoms as a routine viral illness because removal of the federal REMS program ended neutropenia-related laboratory precautions.
options.D: Tell the client to stop future ANC testing but hold clozapine until the sore throat resolves, because infection symptoms now guide treatment more reliably than blood counts.

rationale: Current DailyMed clozapine labeling states that clients who develop a temperature of 101.3°F (38.5°C) or greater during clozapine treatment should have clozapine interrupted and an ANC obtained. The same current labeling recommends ANC testing weekly from initiation through month 6 for clients in the normal ANC range. FDA removed the clozapine REMS effective June 13, 2025, but explicitly states that severe neutropenia remains a serious, potentially fatal risk and that ANC monitoring should continue according to the prescribing information; FDA also tells clients to seek medical care for symptoms that may indicate neutropenia, including fever, chills, and throat infection. Therefore B is correct. A delays the label-directed response to a qualifying fever. C incorrectly treats REMS removal as removal of the underlying neutropenia risk and ANC precautions. D appropriately recognizes that the symptoms matter but incorrectly stops ANC monitoring, which remains recommended and is specifically required in the fever-management pathway.
educational_objective: For a client taking clozapine who develops fever at or above 101.3°F (38.5°C), interrupt clozapine and obtain an ANC promptly; REMS removal did not eliminate the severe-neutropenia risk or ANC monitoring recommendations.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_version_date: Effective May 11, 2026; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-25
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.1 > Management of Clozapine-Treated Patients Who Develop a Fever: interrupt clozapine in patients who develop a temperature of 101.3°F (38.5°C) or greater and obtain an ANC; if ANC is below the specified threshold, initiate appropriate infection workup and treatment. Dosage and Administration §2.3, Table 1: for ANC in the normal range, test weekly from Day 1 through Month 6, every 2 weeks during Months 7–12, and monthly thereafter.
source_claim_supported: A clozapine-treated client with fever of at least 101.3°F (38.5°C) should have clozapine interrupted and an ANC obtained; ANC monitoring remains part of current clozapine treatment.

supporting_sources.document_title: FDA removes risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) program for the antipsychotic drug Clozapine
supporting_sources.version_date: Drug Safety Communication dated August 27, 2025; REMS removal effective June 13, 2025; current FDA page accessed 2026-08-25
supporting_sources.locator: What Is FDA Announcing?: clozapine REMS removed effective June 13, 2025; severe neutropenia risk remains; ANC monitoring can identify neutropenia early; prescribers should continue ANC monitoring according to prescribing information. Patient guidance: contact a health care professional for symptoms of neutropenia including fever or chills and throat infection. What Should Health Care Professionals Do?: counsel patients about severe neutropenia and continue ANC monitoring despite REMS removal.
supporting_sources.claim_supported: The 2025 REMS removal eliminated enrollment/reporting requirements, not the severe-neutropenia risk, symptom escalation, or label-directed ANC monitoring.

blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent data prior to medication administration, educate clients about medications, evaluate client response to medication, and identify actual or potential adverse effects. Related Adverse Effects/Contraindications/Side Effects/Interactions content includes assessing for adverse effects, providing information on when to notify the primary health care provider, and notifying the provider of medication adverse effects or contraindications.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — recognition and management of clozapine-associated severe-neutropenia risk
correction_summary: Rebuilt the stem with a directly sourced fever threshold and rebuilt all four responses to remove distractor-only absolute wording. The corrected item distinguishes removal of the federal REMS administrative program from the continuing clinical requirement for ANC monitoring and label-directed fever management.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Clozapine safety — fever/infection symptoms and severe neutropenia monitoring after REMS removal
audit_findings.stem: PASS — provides a directly sourced qualifying fever threshold, early-treatment timing, and infection symptoms, eliminating ambiguity about whether the label's fever-management instruction applies.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — weekly ANC monitoring is appropriate at 6 weeks, but waiting for the scheduled test conflicts with the explicit fever-management instruction to interrupt clozapine and obtain an ANC.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS — directly follows the current 2026 clozapine label and remains consistent with FDA's post-REMS safety communication; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — REMS removal reduced administrative dispensing requirements but did not eliminate the severe-neutropenia risk, ANC monitoring, or need for evaluation of fever/infection symptoms.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — holding clozapine recognizes the acute concern, but stopping ANC testing contradicts current prescribing information and FDA guidance.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — B is the only response that applies both the current fever threshold and continuing ANC-monitoring requirement without conflating REMS removal with removal of clinical safety precautions.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A delays the required response, C continues treatment based on a false REMS inference, and D abandons required ANC monitoring.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — all options are tightly matched in length and clinical specificity and no distractor-only absolute wording remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes medication adverse-effect recognition, laboratory review, medication education, and provider notification.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether REMS removal could make ANC optional and whether sore throat/fever alone should trigger automatic discontinuation. Current FDA guidance explicitly retains ANC monitoring, and the 2026 DailyMed label specifically directs interruption plus ANC when temperature is at least 101.3°F (38.5°C); the revised stem provides 101.5°F, so B is directly supported without overgeneralizing to lower fevers or permanent discontinuation.
